parsed.why: Adds a school-only facility ban, minors' care ban, surgery-only birth-certificate rule, and a hate-crime statute excluding gender identity; no statewide adult facility rule or documented enforcement, so only modestly below the hostile national framework.

Top protective tier: statewide gender-identity public-accommodations ban, hate-crime coverage, shield law, identity treated in custody including strip searches, X markers. Documented protective machinery working lifts it well above the restrictive national passport and entry layer.

Second-highest risk tier nationally; facility law bars birth-certificate-matching use across all schools and colleges, though unenforced. No statewide gender-identity discrimination statute, marker narrowing, forced-outing rule — local regime clearly below the national average.

Most-protective tier with shield laws and insurance coverage, but a documented state act of placing a trans woman in a men's prison as discipline, plus pending anti-trans ballot initiatives; below the fuller protections of slot 2.

Low-risk tier, governor vetoed bathroom bills, no facility ban, marker change without surgery. Offset by absent state hate-crime coverage, available trans-panic defence, and a dissolved Pride body signalling a deteriorating climate for visible trans presence.
